title: The mountain of herbs
hook: can't remember which herb — brings the mountain

segments.voice: Yesterday: Lanka ablaze, a burning tail, and a humiliation turned into a message. Use what they hand you. Today, a picture of Hanuman you may have seen: a monkey flying, holding a mountain.

Night on the battlefield, later in the story, in the war for Lanka. Rama's brother Lakshmana lies struck down by a terrible weapon, barely breathing. The camp's healer says there's one hope: certain herbs that grow on a mountain in the Himalayas, far to the north. Bring them before sunrise, and he lives. It's a vast distance, and only one of them could cover it that fast. Hanuman goes. He crosses the land in the dark, finds the mountain, lands, and stops. There are plants everywhere, glowing in the night. He doesn't know which ones are the herbs. And the sun will not wait.

So he picks up the whole mountain. He tears off the peak, balances it on one hand, and flies it back to the battlefield. The healer finds the herbs, and Lakshmana lives. That image, Hanuman in the sky with a mountain on his palm, turns up on calendars, temple walls and truck doors. Valmiki's Ramayana tells the herb-mountain journey in its war book, more than once; later tellings, like the race against sunrise, add their own details. Today's word is a name people call him by. Sankat mochan. Sankat means trouble, a crisis, a tight spot. Mochan means release, setting free. The one who frees you from trouble. In Varanasi there's a great temple by that name, and people who are frightened, sick, broke or grieving go and stand before him. Look at his choice. He didn't know exactly what was needed, and he didn't wait until he did. He brought everything. That's seva, your fifteenth word, at full size: service that doesn't do the minimum. Now look back at the week. A baby who reached for the sun. A strength forgotten, and a friend who remembered. A meeting where two disguises fell away. A leap made of small choices. A ring carried across an ocean. A fire turned into a message. And a whole mountain, because one leaf might have been the wrong one. Tomorrow, the Ramayana begins, from the very start.
screen: `HE LIFTS THE WHOLE PEAK.` · `SANKAT MOCHAN — FREER FROM TROUBLE.` · `SEVA AT FULL SIZE.` · `A WEEK WITH HANUMAN.` · then, large: `BRING THE WHOLE MOUNTAIN.`

segments.voice: A seva review: look back over the last week, at where you served someone, with a favor, a meal, time or attention, and where you did the minimum when you could have brought more. No guilt; this isn't a scoreboard. Then hold one person in trouble right now in mind, and ask what bringing the whole mountain would look like for them.
Sankat mochan. The one who frees from trouble: Hanuman, who flew a mountain through the night so a friend would live.
Your line: bring the whole mountain. Service at full size. Day thirty-five, and Hanuman's week is done.
